scope: Theorem 5.1 (Bulk stability) of the manuscript “SLE3 universality for weak finite-range Ising interactions” (preprints/SLE3-universality-for-weak-finite-range-Ising-interactions-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 44a7837e35328259), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 43. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: After increasing s0 if necessary, there is ϵ∗ > 0, depending only on the fixed constants in Proposition 4.7, with the following property. Fix any finite family T of polygonal corridor crossings, polygonal-band circuits, and four-passage square annulus tests. Let N = N(δ) be integers with δ ↓ 0 and infδ δN(δ) > T0(T ), where T0(T ) is sufficiently large that all tests and their fixed collars lie in one planar chart of the physical torus. If ϵ ≤ ϵ∗ and the marks satisfy (5.2), then P ( DT (σ0 , M) = 1 for some T ∈ T ) −→ 0 as δ ↓ 0. (5.4) The threshold ϵ∗ is independent of the family, its polygonal complexity, and all its fixed positive widths. The mesh threshold and the constants in the convergence bound may depend on that geometry. Consequently the pure and perturbed torus laws at the trajectory of Theorem 4.5 have asymp- totically identical joint laws for every such finite family. In particular, pure positive lower bounds for any fixed finite compatible system of signed buffered corridor and circuit events, and pure upper limits for four-passage events, hold for the perturbed law as well.
